questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have visited Australia once before and completely fell in love with its people and culture. Since my initial visit in 2019, the desire to return has been strong. Consequently, there was no doubt in my mind that I had to combine my dream of studying abroad with my love for the country. My choice of Brisbane was based on my familiarity with the city, my fondness for it, and the warmer weather (compared to places like Melbourne) was certainly a significant advantage. Moreover, the courses offered by Brisbane's University of Technology (QUT) aligned perfectly with my field of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: QUT were very accommodating in assisting with all our needs. The first week at the university was entirely dedicated to orientation, providing an opportunity to meet fellow exchange students, engage with student associations, and learn about the university's facilities and support services.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The housing market in Brisbane is incredibly challenging. Due to an overall shortage of available housing in the city, QUT is unable to provide on-campus accommodation. Nevertheless, several "student accommodation" companies operate in the area. I opted to rent a room through Student One, as did the majority of exchange students from Denmark, Sweden, and Norway. However, I do NOT recommend this. The rooms are excessively expensive (8500 kr. for one room in a 5 people appartement), the facilities are worn down, and in desperate need of cleaning. This was a shared experience among all residents at Student One. However, as Student One is situated in the heart of the city, the location is unbeatable.. 

Many attempted to secure private accommodation outside the city, but this proved to be quite challenging due to intense competition on the market. Additionally, most places required a minimum rental period of six months.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you choose student accommodation, it's crucial to be precise about your rental period. While you can extend the duration, shortening it is not possible. I had initially believed exams would conclude in late December, only to discover they finished in early November. Consequently, I found myself obligated to pay an additional month of rent, despite spending that month traveling around.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a master's student, the available courses were somewhat restricted. In Australia, there are numerous prerequisites one must meet to enroll in master's courses. Although this did not turn out to be a significant issue, alleviating my initial concern of not having any courses approved, I still had to provide extensive justification for my qualifications for each of my courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
After securing the exchange spot through KU, I thoroughly examined the QUT course catalogue (available through their website). I systematically reviewed all master's programs and their prerequisites. Subsequently, I began the process of narrowing down the available courses and cross-referencing them with my prior academic qualifications to ensure I met the prerequisites. This is a very time-consuming process, so it's crucial to allocate sufficient time for it. 

I compiled all the relevant course descriptions that I considered important for demonstrating that I indeed met the prerequisites into a PDF file. I then submitted this file along with my course registration.

Despite the fact that a full-time student typically enrolls in only four courses per semester, I opted to apply for six courses. This decision proved beneficial, as I was ultimately approved for four out of the six courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was limited assistance available during the initial course registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contrary to popular belief claiming that it's nearly impossible for master's students to enroll in master's courses in Australia, the reality is quite different. You simply need to invest time in finding relevant courses and provide effective reasonings for your qualification.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level within the field of Communication and IT is relatively low compared to Danish standards.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic standards were notably lower compared to Danish norms. Each time we submitted an assignment, there was a considerable focus on revisiting fundamental academic structures, including APA references. This emphasis on basic skills is something Danish universities presume students to have mastered at the Master's level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a stark contrast. In my home institution, I am accustomed to actively participating in lectures. We frequently engage in shared discussions about a text or a specific topic. However, at my host institution, the expectation was to sit down and listen. Active involvement was reserved solely for the tutorial sessions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:
1. PUN453: Disaster Response and Recovery 
2. AMN436: Developing Cultural Intelligence
3. AMN400: Consumer Insights for Marketing Success
4. AMN420: Manage Advertising

questions.answer:
1. PUN453: Disaster Response and Recovery
 2. AMN436: Developing Cultural Intelligence

Although these courses may not be directly linked to my field of interest, I really enjoyed them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I was surprised by the considerable amount of money allocated to "Personal Spending." Naturally, this varies based on the frequency of trips, social outings, etc.

Furthermore, setting up the apartment incurs significant expenses, including additional kitchen equipment, bedding, pillows, duvets, and more.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol is very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are many student clubs on QUT. I became a part of QUT Surfers and QUT Sport. 
Through these two clubs I was able to go on surf trips, and use the on campus gym facilities. 

In the first couple of months there were many parties as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: QUT surfers is so much fun, however they are very popular. So be ready to sign up for the trips as soon as they are available - it is a great way to meet other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the Gold Coast, visit Byron Bay and Noosa. Go to Sydney, go to Melbourne. Drive up the coast to Cairns. 
Travel as much as possible, but keep the first couple of months free so you have time to explore Brisbane.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people in Australia are exceptionally kind and warm-hearted. Explore the local pubs, attend indie music shows, and catch an Australian stand-up performance. Their charm and hospitality are truly welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it as much as you can, time will simply fly by. 
2. Go to all the social events you can. It might be overwhelming, but it will be worth it. 
3. Save up as much money as possible so you don't have to stress about it while being on exchange. It will be expensive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many amazing people, some of whom I am luck enough to now call my best friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The initial weeks can be challenging as you find yourself alone in a foreign country away from your family. 
However, as you start making friends and explore the local scene, it transforms into the time of your life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
